headline: US Signs $2.45 Billion in Tungsten Deals to Reduce Reliance on China
summary: Washington signed tungsten supply contracts worth up to $2.45 billion to build domestic supply chains ahead of a January 1 Pentagon ban on Chinese-origin tungsten in defense contracting.
why: Tungsten is a critical military material, and trade restrictions create procurement challenges for global defense contractors relying on dominant supply sources.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Federal funding aims to secure defense mineral supply chains separate from Chinese suppliers.
